<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="PartI">PART I</a></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Unless indicated, or unless the context otherwise requires, references in this report to "Gerber" mean Gerber Scientific, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="Item1">ITEM 1.&#160;&#160;BUSINESS</a></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">OVERVIEW</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber Scientific, Inc., through its subsidiaries, develops, manufactures, distributes and services automated equipment and software in three industries worldwide.&#160;&#160;Of its total revenue of $458.4 million for fiscal 2010, Gerber generated $257.2 million in sales of printing equipment, software and related supplies to customers in the sign making and specialty graphics industry; $155.1 million in sales of sophisticated design and cutting equipment and software to customers in the apparel and industrial markets; and $46.1 million in sales of processing equipment, software and related supplies to customers in the ophthalmic lens processing industry.&#160;&#160;Gerber operates manufacturing facilities in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Denmark and China and maintains global sales, distribution and service operations in over 25 countries.&#160;&#160;To maximize its geographic sales coverage, Gerber markets its products through both a direct sales force and independent sales agents located throughout all of the company's domestic and international markets.&#160;&#160;Revenue from international sales, including United States export sales, represented approximately 68 percent of total revenue for fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;As of April 30, 2010, Gerber had approximately 1,950 employees, of whom approximately two-thirds were based outside of the United States.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber's sales strategy emphasizes new product development and expansion within existing geographic markets and into new geographic markets.&#160;&#160;Gerber's product development process focuses on platform development that enables the company to leverage its product innovations with product extensions and add-ons.&#160;&#160;Gerber's long-term growth strategy features geographic expansion in areas such as Asia, particularly in China, and South America.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As part of its business strategy, Gerber also continually reviews and evaluates the risk and opportunities within its existing business segments.&#160;&#160;As a result of these reviews, Gerber may acquire &#8220;bolt-on&#8221; businesses to supplement growth and product development or divest businesses that no longer fit its core long-term growth strategy due to less attractive industry fundamentals or reduced long-term returns.&#160;&#160;In accordance with this strategy, Gerber acquired Yunique Solutions, Inc., a software development company for the apparel markets, in fiscal 2010; Virtek Vision International, Inc., a manufacturer of precision laser-based templating and inspection solutions for industrial material operations, and Gamma Computer Tech Co., Ltd., a China-based manufacturer of equipment for apparel and flexible materials markets, in fiscal 2009; and Data Technology, Inc, a manufacturer of automated cutting hardware for the packaging and graphics industries, in fiscal 2008.&#160;&#160;In fiscal 2010, Gerber sold four non-core businesses, including its laser marking and engraving business unit, FOBA Technology + Services GmbH, or &#8220;FOBA,&#8221; in September 2009.&#160;&#160;FOBA was previously reported within the Apparel and Industrial segment.&#160;&#160;In September 2009, Gerber sold ND Graphics, a Canadian business unit of Gerber Scientific Products.&#160;&#160;Gerber also closed the majority of its Spandex Poland operations during October 2009 and, in April 2010, sold certain assets of its Spandex New Zealand and Gerber Coburn Australia businesses and subsequently ceased substantially all the operating activities related to these businesses.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber pursues a number of initiatives intended to improve its operating efficiency and gross profit margins.&#160;&#160;The focus of this effort is the continuing development of lean manufacturing principles aimed at increasing Gerber's profit margins, including strengthening manufacturing policies and procedures, consolidating and improving supplier relationships, improving inventory methods and reducing inventory, seeking low-cost sourcing opportunities for key parts and components used in the company's newer products, and increasing the company's offerings of higher-margin value-added products.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber Scientific, Inc. was incorporated in Connecticut in 1948.&#160;&#160;Gerber's principal executive offices are located at 83 Gerber Road West, South Windsor, Connecticut 06074, and its main telephone number at that address is (860) 644-1551.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Following is a summary of Gerber's segments, principal products and services.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">SIGN MAKING AND SPECIALTY GRAPHICS</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Sign Making and Specialty Graphics segment consists of Gerber Scientific Products, or "GSP," Spandex and Gerber Innovations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Through GSP and Spandex, Gerber designs, manufactures, services, markets, sells and distributes printing equipment, software and aftermarket supplies to sign making and specialty graphics shops and distributors.&#160;&#160;Customers include small to medium-sized shops with annual revenues ranging from $0.2 million to $3.0 million, larger organizations such as FedEx Kinko&#8217;s, FASTSIGNS and Signs Now, graphic arts professionals, distributors, major corporations and government agencies.&#160;&#160;GSP, headquartered in Connecticut, is the primary manufacturer of equipment offered by this segment.&#160;&#160;The majority of GSP&#8217;s sales are generated through its North American distributor network and Spandex.&#160;&#160;GSP has long-standing relationships with the majority of its distributors and historically has not had any material disruption in sales operations as the result of the termination of any significant distributors.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Spandex, headquartered in Belgium, distributes GSP and other products primarily to the European and Australian sign making markets and other countries through a sub-distribution network.&#160;&#160;Spandex represents many of the industry&#8217;s leading brands and serves approximately 25,000 customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Through Gerber Innovations, Gerber designs, manufactures, sells and services automated equipment for the die making, short run and sample making segments of the packaging industry.&#160;&#160;Gerber Innovations primarily sells directly to end-use customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">No customer of the Sign Making and Specialty Graphics segment individually exceeded ten percent of Gerber&#8217;s consolidated sales for fiscal 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Principal Products and Services Portfolio</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GSP manufactures the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GERBER Solara ion</font>&#8482;, a wide-format ultraviolet, or "UV," inkjet printer for digital imaging markets.&#160;&#160;The digital imaging markets continue to evolve as a result of rapid technological advances and as sign shops continue to transition from thermal printing to digital technology.&#160;&#160;The <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Solara ion </font>offers advanced performance in UV inkjet printing by using Gerber's patent pending Cold Fire Cure&#8482; process and GerberCAT&#8482; cationic ink.&#160;&#160;The Cold Fire Cure process offers greater material compatibility and, due to its lower energy output and heat generation, extends the life of curing lamps used in UV printing.&#160;&#160;GerberCAT cationic ink enables printing on a wide array of both rigid and flexible substrates with high-quality adhesion, abrasion resistance and color output.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Although market demand for inkjet printers is outpacing that of thermal printers, Gerber maintains a leadership position in the thermal print market.&#160;&#160;Due to its large installed base of easy-to-use thermal printers and the outdoor durability of the signs produced, Gerber believes that there is a continuing role for thermal imaging printers and a sustainable demand for aftermarket</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">5</font></div>

</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">supplies.&#160;&#160;The <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GERBER EDGE&#174; FX, </font>a thermal imaging system, is an easy-to-use solution for sign makers, screen printers and other graphic professionals seeking to quickly produce highly-customized short-run graphics.&#160;&#160;The EDGE FX uses heat and pressure to infuse durable resin pigments to more than 30 different printing material substrates, produces graphics with high-quality images, and dries instantly, with no waste, odor, harmful emissions, or need for ventilation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other significant products of this segment include plotters, routers, computer-aided design, or &#8220;CAD,&#8221; computer-aided manufacturing, or &#8220;CAM,&#8221; cutting systems and software.&#160;&#160;GSP&#8217;s plotters are used to cut signs or graphic forms from vinyl substrates.&#160;&#160;Routers are used to make 3-D cuts in other signage materials, such as wood or plastic.&#160;&#160;The Gerber M Series is a cutting system designed for wide-format graphics that provides manufacturers of graphics, signs and other rigid and flexible printed media with versatile tools to cut, rout and crease a wide variety of substrates.&#160;&#160;GSP's CAD and CAM cutting systems are used to produce dies boards and samples and for short-run production for packaging companies in the corrugated and folding carton industries.&#160;&#160;Products consist of sample making and digital die cutting systems, die tool production systems and rotary and flat rule die processing systems, which incorporate knife, laser and waterjet cutting technologies.&#160;&#160;GSP software is used to design signs and specialty graphics, as well as to manage printing and cutting processes.&#160;&#160;Although GSP offers several proprietary software programs depending on customer needs, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">OMEGA&#8482; 4.0 </font>is GSP's most powerful design and production software and represents the most significant software product within this segment.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Sales of the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Solara ion</font> and related aftermarket materials, thermal imaging systems and other significant products or software did not individually exceed ten percent of consolidated revenue for fiscal 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Aftermarket supplies sold by this segment accounted for approximately 48 percent of Gerber&#8217;s consolidated revenue for fiscal 2010, 46 percent of consolidated revenue for fiscal 2009 and 44 percent of consolidated revenue for fiscal 2008.&#160;&#160;GSP offers a wide range of aftermarket supplies such as color foils (which is the "ink" used in thermal printers), adhesive-backed vinyls, banner materials and inks for inkjet printers.&#160;&#160;Cartridges include the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GerberGauge&#8482; </font>marking system, a proprietary system that uses radio-frequency identification, or "RFID," technology to estimate the remaining foil length on cartridges to help prevent unexpected run-out and wasted foil and material, while improving workflow.&#160;&#160;GSP also offers a variety of durable and flexible UV curable inks for inkjet products.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Raw Materials</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GSP obtains critical materials from four primary suppliers and original equipment manufacturers, or "OEMs."&#160;&#160;GSP purchases cast vinyl from a supplier with which GSP has a long-standing relationship.&#160;&#160;GSP purchases color foils from a leading European supplier for a wide range of industries.&#160;&#160;Thermal transfer UV print heads and cationic inks are supplied by Japanese manufacturers.&#160;&#160;GSP does not currently have written supply agreements with these suppliers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As a distributor, Spandex purchases critical products from various suppliers, including GSP and OEMs.&#160;&#160;In some cases, Spandex uses only one source of supply for certain&#160;products.&#160;&#160;Historically, Spandex has not experienced significant difficulties in obtaining timely deliveries of these&#160;products.&#160;&#160;Increased demand or lack of availability for these products in the future could result in&#160;shipment delays that might adversely affect Spandex's business.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Should it experience delays in obtaining raw materials or products from any suppliers to this segment, Gerber believes it could develop internal or external alternatives, although it may be difficult to replace the marketing advantages of using certain supplier brands.&#160;&#160;In the near term, Gerber does not foresee any potential lack in availability or sourcing of critical products that would have a material adverse effect on this segment.&#160;&#160;Gerber maintains contingent insurance coverage in the event specified suppliers are unable to perform their obligations due to certain insured events.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GSP faces competition in sign making markets for its products, particularly with respect to the sale of inkjet products and aftermarket supplies.&#160;&#160;GSP principally competes on the basis of the comprehensiveness of its product line, product quality and availability, service and pricing.&#160;&#160;GSP believes it has a competitive advantage by offering its customers a complete start-to-finish system for digital design, printing and production products and comprehensive engineered solutions for durable vinyl-cutting, digital color printing and dimensional signage needs, and advises customers on how to maximize their return on investment through the purchase of GSP products.</font></div>

<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">6</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As an international supplier, Spandex competes with both larger and smaller companies, depending on the country and market segment.&#160;&#160;While Spandex is one of the largest international suppliers in the durable outdoor graphics marketplace, it competes in some geographic markets with companies that are considerably larger than Spandex, including PaperlinX Ltd, Antalis International and Oc&#233; N.V.&#160;&#160;In addition, demand in recent years for digital wide format inkjet and aftermarket supplies has been increasing in the markets served by Spandex, which has led to increased competition from equipment suppliers and aftermarket distributors of these products.&#160;&#160;Spandex competes on the basis of its market and technical knowledge, supplier relationships and supply chain infrastructure, and a wide array of products and support services.&#160;&#160;Most of Spandex's customers are small sign shops that find Spandex's ability to meet most of their product needs appealing.&#160;&#160;Spandex relies heavily on its ability to provide competitive product offerings from both GSP and strategic OEM providers.&#160;&#160;Spandex competes with some of its suppliers that use distribution networks and also employ direct sales forces, which can lead to competition with Spandex's product offerings.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">APPAREL AND INDUSTRIAL</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Apparel and Industrial operating segment (formerly referred to as the Apparel and Flexible Materials segment) markets its products through the Gerber Technology, or "GT," business unit.&#160;&#160;GT develops, manufactures, distributes and services sophisticated design and cutting equipment and software for over 22,000<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>customers in apparel and industrial markets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GT&#8217;s comprehensive suite of products can be used by its customers as integrated solutions throughout the design and manufacturing process.&#160;&#160;These products include product life cycle management and product data management software, CAD and CAM equipment and software solutions, laser projection systems for composite assembly, prefabricated construction and quality control systems.&#160;&#160;GT&#8217;s products and software offerings are designed to enhance its customers' manufacturing processes and efficiencies from design through production by reducing turnaround times, material waste and labor costs.&#160;&#160;GT offers specialized solutions to manufacturers of sewn and flexible goods for a broad range of end markets, including apparel and retail (67 percent of segment revenue), industrial and aerospace composites (12 percent of segment revenue), transportation interiors (10 percent of segment revenue) and upholstered furniture (11 percent of segment revenue).&#160;&#160;Headquartered in Connecticut, GT engineers, manufactures and distributes its products throughout the Americas, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.&#160;&#160;No customer of the Apparel and Industrial segment individually accounted for more than ten percent of Gerber&#8217;s consolidated sales for fiscal 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GT maintains regional offices, agents or distributors in over 125 countries.&#160;&#160;In certain geographies, GT utilizes third-party sales agents and distributors, Gerber believes that its longstanding network provides a significant benefit in certain markets, as these networks are staffed with knowledgeable individuals who speak the local language and have a thorough understanding of the local market.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The migration of apparel manufacturing to lower labor cost areas has displaced some opportunities for GT equipment sales in North America and Europe.&#160;&#160;These markets, however, continue to represent a significant recurring revenue source for GT due to the large installed base of GT's products, which require service, software subscriptions and aftermarket supplies.&#160;&#160;GT also continues to experience demand from North America and Europe for apparel lifecycle design and development software and GT's industrial software and hardware solutions, including its technical textile, composite material and leather cutting systems.&#160;&#160;GT believes that the migration of flexible materials manufacturing to lower labor cost areas and the emergence of new market and supply-chain trends within the apparel industry provide GT with continuing growth opportunities.&#160;&#160;To capitalize on these trends, GT has developed a sales and service network in Asia, including approximately 25 sales and service centers in China as of April 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;GT expects to derive much of its future revenue growth from sales to markets in Asia, particularly China, India and Vietnam.&#160;&#160;China is GT's fastest growing market and the world's largest apparel-producing nation.&#160;&#160;Sales within greater China accounted for $23.4 million of GT's fiscal 2010 revenue, $18.5 million of GT's fiscal 2009 revenue and $30.5 million of GT&#8217;s fiscal 2008 revenue.&#160;&#160;Gerber believes that the decline in revenue from fiscal 2008 levels within greater China was attributable to economic factors, as apparel manufacturers in China were significantly impacted by the global recession and appear to have slowed capital equipment investments, and was not indicative of a change in GT's market share.&#160;&#160;Revenue in China began to recover during fiscal 2010 and is expected to return to pre-recession levels.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The evolving strategy for GT is focused on growth.&#160;&#160;During the last two fiscal years, bolt-on acquisitions targeted specific markets and products for GT, including Gerber&#8217;s November 2009 acquisition of Yunique Solutions, Inc., or &#8220;Yunique,&#8221; its September 2008 acquisition of Gamma Computer Tech Co., Ltd., or "Gamma," and its October 2008 acquisition of Virtek Vision International, Inc., or &#8220;Virtek.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Yunique, located in New York, is a software development company serving apparel and flexible materials industries and is expected to enhance Gerber&#8217;s existing product lifecycle management and product data</font></div>

<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">customer training, technical support and comprehensive maintenance and specialized support services.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">No single product or software offering accounted for more than ten percent of Gerber&#8217;s consolidated revenue for fiscal 2010, 2009 or 2008.&#160;&#160;As a percentage of consolidated revenue, GT&#8217;s service revenue represented 11 percent for fiscal 2010, 10 percent for fiscal 2009 and did not exceed 10 percent of consolidated revenue for fiscal 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GT&#8217;s software product lines, which are enterprise-wide applications, allow for global management of production activities and facilitate communication of measurement specifications, construction details, costing and bill of material information among apparel and other flexible materials designers, raw materials suppliers, makers of the materials and retailers.&#160;&#160;PLM software assists in accelerating the speed of products from concept to market, which is critically important in the apparel industry due to shorter fashion cycles.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">YuniquePLM </font>and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Fashion Lifecycle Management&#174;, </font>or "FLM," are GT's brands for PLM, which are designed to accelerate products to market with configurable workflow functionality.&#160;&#160;PLM software systems reduce lead times, increase the accuracy of prototyping and improve the quality of information flow along the production cycle chain.&#160;&#160;GT's <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Web</font>PDM&#8482; software solution has been implemented by over 1,200 customers worldwide, which hold more than 19,000 PDM software licenses.&#160;&#160;Other software packages offered include conceptual design software, advanced CAD pattern-making software and marker making and nesting software.&#160;&#160;Virtek offers software for the prefabricated construction industry and the aerospace composite and other assembly industries to control their projectors and assist in the projection of images and design of the manufactured components.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GT's spreading and cutting equipment is designed to reduce labor costs of previously labor-intensive functions, while minimizing material waste and assembly error.&#160;&#160;GT's line of spreaders are marketed as <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GERBERspreaders&#8482;</font> and deliver tension-free spreading of materials at speeds of up to 100 meters per minute.&#160;&#160;The XLs line of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GERBERspreaders</font> is designed for apparel manufacturers in developing markets that require effective automation solutions at affordable prices.&#160;&#160;GT's cutting systems increase operating efficiencies in soft goods manufacturing by cutting parts with a high degree of accuracy from single and multiple layers of flexible materials, such as textiles, leathers, vinyls, plastics, fiberglass and advanced composites.&#160;&#160;GT's cutting systems perform faster and more efficiently and with greater precision than the traditional methods of hand-cutting or die-cutting.&#160;&#160;The GT cutters are offered in single-, medium- and high-ply models and marketed as <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GERBERcutter&#174;.&#160;&#160;</font>GT also offers a high-ply cutting system, the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">XLc7000</font>, which is specifically designed for apparel manufacturers in developing markets that require effective automation solutions at affordable prices.&#160;&#160;The Z7 <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GERBERcutter</font>, targeted at automotive, industrial and composite markets, combines precision with efficiency in cutting demanding materials to tight tolerances.&#160;&#160;GT also offers the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Taurus&#8482;</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Taurus X Series</font> automated leather cutting systems with hide scanning, flaw capture and multiple nesting package capabilities.&#160;&#160;These cutters appeal to industrial customers, particularly in the transportation sector.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Customers use GT's plotters to produce accurate design prints on industrial-width paper for placement on fabric or other materials to provide information relative to cutting and downstream operations.&#160;&#160;The most recent product launched in the plotter product line was produced in China using the supply chain resources from the recently acquired Gamma operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Virtek line of products for customers in both aerospace composite and prefabricated construction industries include LPS7</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">laser projectors optimized for laser templating applications.&#160;&#160;Also offered by Virtek are LaserQC products that quickly perform inspection for sheet metal, gasket manufacturing and other industries producing flat parts.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GT&#8217;s products and software are serviced subsequent to the initial sale through annual maintenance software and service contracts and through replenishment of consumable parts such as cutting blades and spare parts.&#160;&#160;In fiscal 2010, GT launched <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GERBERconnect</font>&#8482;, which allows remote monitoring of its systems at customer locations.&#160;&#160;This new offering allows Gerber to proactively contact customers to take preventative maintenance steps to ensure greater uptime and operating efficiency.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Raw Materials</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GT purchases materials, such as computers, computer peripherals, electronic parts and equipment, from numerous suppliers.&#160;&#160;Many of these materials are incorporated directly into GT's manufactured products, while others require additional processing.&#160;&#160;In some cases, GT uses only one supplier for certain materials.&#160;&#160;Historically, GT has not experienced significant difficulties in timely deliveries of these materials.&#160;&#160;Increased demand or future lack of materials availability could result in production delays that might adversely affect GT's business.&#160;&#160;GT's management believes that, if required, it could establish alternative suppliers for its material requirements.&#160;&#160;In the near term, GT's management does not foresee that a potential lack of materials, components or supplies availability from any particular source would have a material adverse effect on its overall business.&#160;&#160;Gerber maintains contingent insurance coverage in the event specified suppliers are unable to perform their obligations due to certain insured events.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GT is a leading provider in its geographic markets of computer-controlled material spreading and cutting systems, PLM and PDM solutions and pattern-making, grading and nesting software.&#160;&#160;GT faces intense competition in each of these product lines from companies based in Europe, including Lectra, Bullmer and Optitex.&#160;&#160;GT's product range and international distribution network enables GT to support key customer accounts that shift production and sourcing activities around the world.&#160;&#160;Virtek is a leading provider for laser and templating solutions.&#160;&#160;Virtek&#8217;s primary competitor is SL Laser in Europe.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">OPHTHALMIC LENS PROCESSING</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Ophthalmic Lens Processing segment, operating through Gerber Coburn, or "GC," designs, manufactures, markets and services equipment, software and supplies used in processing prescription eyewear.&#160;&#160;GC's product line includes computer integrated equipment for lens production steps such as blocking, fining, polishing, hard coating, finishing and inspecting; start-to-finish lab management software; and the related supplies used in lens processing.&#160;&#160;GC, headquartered in Connecticut, serves wholesale lens production laboratories, retail eyewear chains and independent eye care professionals throughout North America, Europe and rest of world international markets.&#160;&#160;GC distributes its products directly in the United States and Canada.&#160;&#160;In its other international markets, GC uses a combination of a direct sales force and independent agents to maximize geographic coverage.&#160;&#160;GC also participates in industry trade shows in the Americas, Europe and Asia, which often provide it with a significant source of new sales leads.&#160;&#160;No customer of the Ophthalmic Lens Processing segment individually accounted for more than ten percent of Gerber&#8217;s consolidated sales for fiscal 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Growth within this segment is likely to come from geographic expansion, the launch of new products and market recovery.&#160;&#160;Gerber believes substantial geographic growth opportunities are emerging in Asia, Eastern Europe and Latin America, as these countries continue to develop the infrastructure to perform sophisticated eye exams for a growing middle class.&#160;&#160;Gerber believes that this consumer group is likely to seek more features for prescription eyewear, such as multi-focal lenses, which is expected to create additional demand for the types of products offered by GC.&#160;&#160;Advanced technology within this segment includes the production of free-form (or digital) lenses.&#160;&#160;Free-form lens processing allows the production of a progressive (no-line multi-focal) lens surface through machining rather than traditional casting or molding processes, and enables the lens laboratory to provide other value-added characteristics to the lens.&#160;&#160;GC's <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Advanced Lens Processing System</font>, which was introduced in fiscal 2009, is positioned to meet demand resulting from this market trend.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Principal Products and Services Portfolio</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GC's equipment offerings consist of lens surfacing equipment, hard coating equipment, finishing equipment and lens inspection equipment.&#160;&#160;Lens surfacing equipment includes computer-controlled surfacing equipment to create precise curves on the lenses.</font></div>

<br>

<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GC offers the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">DTL Generator with Cut-to-Polish and Free-Form options</font>, which is an expandable high-speed system targeted at the wholesale laboratory market.&#160;&#160;GC also offers lens blocking products designed for high throughput manufacturing environments.&#160;&#160;In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2010, GC launched a new, eco-friendly E2G Blocking System for the wholesale market.&#160;&#160;The system consists of the E2G blocker, new surface blocks, a deblocker, and a proprietary environmentally safe medium called Onyx-Bond&#8482;.&#160;&#160;For lens fining and polishing applications, GC markets the CMX-50 cylinder machine to the wholesale laboratory market and the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Acuity </font>product<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>to the retail segment of the market.&#160;&#160;The MAAT Polishing System is offered for cut-to-polish and free-form lens production.&#160;&#160;GC's <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Advanced Lens Processing System</font>, or "ALPS," includes the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">DTL Generator with Cut-to-Polish and Free-Form options</font> and the MAAT Polishing System, and enables free-form (or digital) lens production.&#160;&#160;GC&#8217;s lens finishing equipment for retail markets is distributed in collaboration with Essilor International, S.A., an ophthalmic products manufacturer.&#160;&#160;For finishing in the laboratory environment, GC distributes industrial and automated products, including the Weco Verifier and the 950 and 990 Blockless Edging Systems.&#160;&#160;GC sells an ophthalmic lens processing system, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Premier Lab</font>&#8482;, designed for retail lens processing.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Premier Lab</font> is a compact, full service laboratory for processing CR39, high-index and polycarbonate lenses.&#160;&#160;A <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Premier Lab</font> includes a frame tracer, blocking system, surface generator, finer and polisher, coating system, finishing system and related software.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GC's software is an important component of its comprehensive solutions, especially for small laboratories.&#160;&#160;Software offerings owned or distributed by GC range from simple remote tracing with Innovations Lite&#8482; software to a more comprehensive software package such as Innovations&#8482; Standard software.&#160;&#160;GC provides on-site software installation, training and support in all of its geographic markets through its internal network of local service specialists.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2008, Gerber sold its rights to the Innovations software product and retained the right to distribute the product on a worldwide basis.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Aftermarket supplies are used by GC&#8217;s customers during the operation of lens equipment.&#160;&#160;These aftermarket supplies offer a significant recurring revenue opportunity subsequent to the initial sale of equipment.&#160;&#160;Certain aftermarket supplies are sold with a right to return.&#160;&#160;Revenue on aftermarket supplies that is sold with a right to return is recognized upon shipment and an estimate for expected returns is recorded at the same time based upon historical experience and current economic factors.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenue from sales of the various classes of GC&#8217;s products, software and services did not exceed ten percent of Gerber&#8217;s consolidated revenue for fiscal 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Raw Materials</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GC purchases materials from numerous suppliers and acts as a distributor for third-party OEM products.&#160;&#160;Many of the purchased materials are incorporated directly into GC's manufactured products, while others require additional processing.&#160;&#160;GC has not experienced significant difficulties in obtaining timely deliveries from suppliers or OEM providers.&#160;&#160;Increased demand for these materials or products or future lack of availability could result in production delays that might adversely affect GC's business.&#160;&#160;GC's management believes that, if required, it could develop alternative sources of supply for the materials and sourced products used.&#160;&#160;In the near term, GC's management does not foresee that a potential lack of materials, components, supplies or product availability from any particular source would have a material adverse effect on its overall business.&#160;&#160;Gerber maintains contingent insurance coverage in the event specified suppliers are unable to perform their obligations due to certain insured events.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GC's principal competitors in the high volume laboratory market segment are Satisloh GmbH, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Essilor International, S.A. and Schneider GmbH. Principal competitors in the retail and eye care professionals segment include Nidek Inc., Briot International and AIT Industries.&#160;&#160;GC competes principally on the basis of product innovation and comprehensiveness, onsite service support, and distribution capabilities.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber's success depends, in part, on its intellectual property rights relating to its products, production processes and other operations.&#160;&#160;Gerber relies on a combination of trade secret, nondisclosure and other contractual arrangements, and patent, trademark and copyright laws, to protect its proprietary rights.&#160;&#160;Intellectual property rights may be challenged by third parties and may not exclude competitors from using the same or similar technologies, brands or works.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber owns and has applications pending for a number of patents in the United States and other countries covering many of its products and systems.&#160;&#160;&#160;Gerber's existing patents expire at various dates through 2027.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has granted Gerber federal registrations for many of its trademarks.&#160;&#160;Federal registration of trademarks is effective for as long as Gerber continues to uses the trademarks and renew their registrations.&#160;&#160;Gerber does not generally register any of its copyrights with the U.S. Copyright Office, but relies on the protection afforded to such copyrights by the U.S. Copyright Act.&#160;&#160;That law provides protection to authors of original works, whether published or unpublished, and whether registered or unregistered.&#160;&#160;Gerber enters into confidentiality agreements with its employees and some third parties and limits access to and distribution of its proprietary information.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">SEASONALITY</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">GSP and Spandex's sales of equipment and aftermarket supplies are affected by seasonality in the sign industry, especially during the fall and spring periods of North America and Europe, when demand customarily peaks.&#160;&#160;Sales by GT and GC are not significantly impacted by seasonality trends.&#160;&#160;Gerber typically realizes the largest portion of its annual revenue during the fourth fiscal quarter.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Developing new and innovative products and broadening the application of established products are important to Gerber's operating results.&#160;&#160;Research and development expenses were $18.5 million for fiscal 2010, $21.1 million for fiscal 2009 and $26.2 million for fiscal 2008.&#160;&#160;Gerber develops and designs new products to assist its customers in reducing costs and improving efficiencies to enhance and maintain their end market positions.&#160;&#160;The lower expenses in fiscal 2010 and 2009 as compared with fiscal 2008 reflected the impact of workforce reductions, although the decreased expenses were partially offset by incremental development costs incurred by acquired companies.&#160;&#160;Fiscal 2011 research and development spending is expected to be limited to strategic new product development and sustaining engineering of existing products, which includes potential design changes to lower product costs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">FINANCING ACTIVITIES</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber has agreements with major financial services institutions, or "lessors," to assist Gerber's customers, or "lessees," in obtaining lease financing to purchase Gerber's equipment.&#160;&#160;Equipment is typically leased for periods of two to six years.&#160;&#160;The equipment sold collateralizes the lease receivables.&#160;&#160;In the event of default by the lessee, Gerber has a liability to the financial services institution under recourse provisions once the institution repossesses the equipment from the lessee and returns it to</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">None of Gerber's principal businesses is directly subject to government regulation that is material to that business.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a name="Item1A">ITEM 1A.&#160;&#160;RISK FACTORS</a></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, you should carefully consider the following factors, which could materially affect our business, financial condition or future results.&#160;&#160;The risks described below are not the only risks facing our company.&#160;&#160;Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial also may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Company-Wide Risks</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If Gerber is unable to continue to develop and commercialize new technologies and products, it may experience a decrease in demand for its products or its products could become obsolete.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber believes that its ability to develop or acquire new technologies is crucial to the company's success.&#160;&#160;Gerber may not be successful in enhancing existing products or developing or acquiring new products and technologies that will achieve desired or expected levels of market acceptance.&#160;&#160;New products may require incremental start-up costs associated with new product launches.&#160;&#160;In addition, new products must respond to technological changes and evolving industry standards.&#160;&#160;Gerber's operating results could be adversely affected if it is unable, for technological or other reasons, to develop and introduce new products in a timely manner in response to changing market conditions or customer requirements, or if it introduces products late to the market, thereby resulting in missed opportunities in dynamic, fast-moving markets or resulting in a failure to achieve market acceptance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Any failure by Gerber to adequately manage future new product introductions could adversely affect Gerber's sales of existing products.&#160;&#160;As new or enhanced products are introduced, Gerber must successfully manage the transition from older products to minimize disruption in customers' ordering patterns, avoid excessive levels of older product inventories and ensure that sufficient supplies of new products can be delivered to meet customers' demands.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber's businesses could suffer as a result of manufacturers' or suppliers' inability or unwillingness to supply Gerber with systems, parts or aftermarket supplies on time and to specifications.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber relies upon domestic and international manufacturers and suppliers for certain hardware and aftermarket supplies, which are manufactured to Gerber's specifications.&#160;&#160;The inability or unwillingness of a manufacturer or supplier to ship such products in a timely manner or to meet quality standards could cause Gerber to miss customers' delivery date requirements for those products, which could result in the cancellation of orders, refusal to accept deliveries, lost customers, product returns or voluntary reductions in purchase prices.&#160;&#160;Any one of those consequences could have an adverse effect on Gerber's operating</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">12</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">results and financial condition.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber continually engages in the development of new and enhanced products in an effort to develop incremental sales and improve gross margins.&#160;&#160;The industries in which Gerber operates are highly competitive and subject to significant and rapid technological change.&#160;&#160;In some periods, Gerber's revenue growth depends on outsourcing arrangements with OEMs to augment its product lines.&#160;&#160;If OEMs are not able to supply products reliably, in a timely manner, or at a competitive cost, Gerber's business may suffer.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber may not benefit from its acquisition strategy.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber&#8217;s level of debt and interest payment obligations may limit its ability to compete and expose it to interest rate risk to the extent of its variable-rate debt.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Because borrowings under Gerber&#8217;s revolving credit facility accrue interest at variable rates, Gerber&#8217;s interest expense could increase if interest rates increase and it is not able to manage its related exposure through derivative financial instruments.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber may be unable to comply with the financial covenants in its credit agreement unless it continues to generate sufficient operating cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber&#8217;s ability to comply with the financial covenants under the credit agreement for its $75 million senior secured revolving credit facility depends primarily on its ability to generate sufficient operating cash flows.&#160;&#160;Under its credit agreement, Gerber is subject to a maximum funded debt to consolidated EBITDA ratio, a minimum interest coverage ratio, a maximum capital expenditures covenant and a minimum asset coverage covenant, all as defined for purposes of the credit agreement.&#160;&#160;Industry conditions and financial, business and other factors, including those Gerber identifies as risk factors in this report, will affect its ability to generate the cash flows it needs to meet those financial covenants.&#160;&#160;Gerber&#8217;s failure to meet the covenants could result in a default and acceleration of repayment of the indebtedness under its revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;The credit agreement contains subjective acceleration clauses under which, upon the occurrence of a change in Gerber's financial condition, business or operations considered by the lenders to be materially adverse to Gerber, the lenders may cause amounts due under the agreement to become immediately due and payable.&#160;&#160;If the maturity of Gerber&#8217;s indebtedness were accelerated, it would not have sufficient funds to pay such indebtedness.&#160;&#160;In such event, Gerber&#8217;s lenders would be entitled to proceed against the collateral securing the indebtedness, which includes substantially all of Gerber&#8217;s assets, to the extent permitted by the credit agreement and applicable law.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Covenants under Gerber&#8217;s credit agreement may restrict its future operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber&#8217;s senior secured revolving credit facility agreement imposes operating and financial restrictions that limit Gerber&#8217;s discretion on some business matters, which could make it more difficult for Gerber to expand, finance its operations, pursue its acquisition strategy, and engage in other business activities that may be in its interest.&#160;&#160;These restrictions, which include compliance with financial covenants, limit the ability of Gerber and its subsidiaries to:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber may incur indebtedness in addition to the foregoing indebtedness.&#160;&#160;Any additional indebtedness it may incur in the future could subject Gerber to similar or even more restrictive conditions.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If Gerber is unable to raise additional capital, its ability to expand its business and to meet its obligations may be limited.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The development and expansion of Gerber&#8217;s business will require substantial investment.&#160;&#160;If Gerber chooses to accelerate the expansion of its business or undertake significant acquisitions of other businesses, Gerber may require additional capital.&#160;&#160;If Gerber cannot obtain additional equity or debt financing for such purposes on acceptable terms, the company could be at a competitive disadvantage relative to competitors with significant capital or the ability to raise significant capital for expansion.&#160;&#160;The terms of any financing Gerber does obtain will be restricted by the terms of its existing debt agreement and may be burdensome to the company.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">14</font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Credit market risk could adversely affect Gerber's investments, Gerber's ability to raise additional capital and the ability of its customers and suppliers to obtain financing needed to transact business with Gerber.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Distress in credit and financial markets has reduced liquidity and credit availability and increased volatility in prices of securities.&#160;&#160;Credit market risk could also adversely impact the performance of investments in Gerber's pension plans, resulting in unrealized temporary losses, realized losses, other-than-temporary impairment charges or a decline in the funded status of the pension plan.&#160;&#160;Investments subject to credit market risk as of April 30, 2010 include investments held on behalf of Gerber's nonqualified supplemental pension plan in rabbi trust and within the Gerber Scientific, Inc. and Participating Subsidiaries Pension Plan.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Credit market risk could negatively impact Gerber's lenders' ability and willingness to fund the committed amount under its revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;In addition, Gerber&#8217;s ability to access the debt and equity markets may be restricted at a time when it would like, or need, to access such markets, which could have an adverse effect on Gerber&#8217;s flexibility to react to changing economic and business conditions.&#160;&#160;The disruptions in the financial markets have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on the market value of Gerber&#8217;s common stock, which could make it more difficult or costly for the company to raise capital through an offering of its equity securities.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Credit market risk could negatively impact customers' ability to obtain external financing to purchase Gerber's products and suppliers' ability to deliver goods to Gerber in accordance with their commitments.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Unforeseen environmental costs may adversely affect Gerber's future earnings.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber operates and competes on a global basis and must conform to applicable environmental, health and safety, or "EH&amp;S," laws and regulations wherever the company operates, and in some cases, wherever its products are sold.&#160; If Gerber fails to comply with any present or future EH&amp;S laws or regulations, it could incur liabilities, including monetary, civil and criminal penalties and liabilities resulting from the suspension of sales of noncompliant products.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">EH&amp;S laws and regulations, which generally affect Gerber's manufacturing and warehousing operations, regulate the storage, use, discharge and disposal of chemicals employed in manufacturing products. New and emerging EH&amp;S legislation is aimed at regulating the chemical composition of finished products and establishing requirements for the end-of-life collection, recovery, reuse, recycling, treatment and environmentally sound disposal of the products themselves. Such legislation has recently gone into effect within the European Union and similar legislation for China.&#160; As these new EH&amp;S laws and regulations emerge across the global community, it can be difficult to assess how they will be interpreted, implemented and enforced by regulators within the various countries and jurisdictions, and to predict the potential costs of noncompliance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Uncertainty continues to exist with respect to some effective European Union legislation.&#160; One European Union directive restricts the use of certain hazardous substances in some electrical and electronic equipment, while another directive mandates requirements in the collection, reuse, recycling, treatment and environmentally sound disposal of certain electrical and electronic equipment at the end of its useful life.&#160; If alleged to be in noncompliance with this or other European Union directives affecting finished products, Gerber could be required to pay significant legal fees in defense of its positions and, if unsuccessful, could be required to suspend sales of noncompliant products within the relevant European Union member states.&#160; The suspension of product sales could cause the breach of contractual obligations and result in Gerber being directly or indirectly liable for costs, penalties or third-party claims.&#160; A sustained finding of noncompliance could additionally require Gerber to incur significant expenses associated with the redesign or reengineering of products or manufacturing processes, or incur expenses associated with the possible recall of any noncompliant product or the management of historical waste products.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber may not effectively protect its intellectual property.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Gerber's operational and legal controls to help to secure its intellectual property may not prove to be effective in all circumstances.&#160;&#160;Gerber may not be able to protect key intellectual property, particularly in some international markets in which it operates.&#160;&#160;Because certain of Gerber's manufacturing operations are located outside of the United States, some of Gerber's patented products may be reverse-engineered and rebuilt by a local competitor.&#160;&#160;In some countries, such as China, Gerber's intellectual property rights may not be legally protected.</font></div>
