<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In connection with the acquisition of Yunique (see Note 5), a liability was recognized for the Company&#8217;s estimate of the fair value of contingent consideration on the acquisition date based on probability-based forecasted revenue.&#160;&#160;Any change in fair value of the contingent consideration subsequent to the acquisition date will be recognized in the statement of operations.&#160;&#160;This fair value measurement is based on significant inputs not observed in the market and thus represents a Level 3 measurement.&#160;&#160;Level 3 instruments are valued based on unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity and reflect the Company&#8217;s own assumptions concerning future revenue of Yunique in measuring fair value.&#160;&#160;A change in the estimated probabilities of revenue achievement could have a material effect on the statement of operations and balance sheets in the period of change.&#160;&#160;There were no changes to the level 3 liability during the fiscal year ended April 30, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In connection with the sale of ND Graphics, the Company remained a guarantor under a lease for ND Graphic&#8217;s headquarters facility in Toronto, Canada. This lease expires during the fiscal year ending April 30, 2018.&#160;&#160;The remaining undiscounted monthly lease payments were $2.3 million as of the sale date.&#160;&#160;The fair value of this liability of $0.7 million was recorded in Other long-term liabilities on the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The fair value of the $0.7 million liability was estimated using a probability based discounted cash flow analysis for the probability of non-performance by ND Graphics.&#160;&#160;As of April 30, 2010, there was no existing default or indication of a prospective default by ND Graphics under the lease.&#160;&#160;There were no changes to the level 3 liability during the fiscal year ended April 30, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The above fair values were computed based on quoted market prices or an estimate of the amount received or paid to terminate or settle the agreement, as applicable.&#160;&#160;The fair values of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, accounts payable and accrued expenses approximate the carrying amounts due to their short-term nature.&#160;&#160;All of the Company&#8217;s outstanding debt accrues interest at variable interest rates.&#160;&#160;As the underlying interest rates are believed to represent market rates, the carrying</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Note 17.&#160;&#160;Segment Reporting</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Reportable segments are determined based on management's evaluation of the business units.&#160;&#160;Each business unit sells internationally as well as within the United States.&#160;&#160;The Sign Making and Specialty Graphics segment manufactures and distributes computer-controlled production systems, software and aftermarket supplies sold to a diversified customer base in the sign making and specialty graphics industries.&#160;&#160;This segment is comprised of the Gerber Scientific Products and Spandex business units.&#160;&#160;The Apparel and Industrial (formerly Apparel and Flexible Materials) segment manufactures and distributes computer-controlled production systems and software for product design, spreading, labeling, cutting, and handling of flexible materials such as fabrics and composites.&#160;&#160;The Apparel and Industrial segment's customer base is in the apparel, aerospace, automotive, furniture and other industries.&#160;&#160;The results of Yunique, Gamma and Virtek are included within the Apparel and Industrial segment from the respective dates of acquisition.&#160;&#160;See Notes 1 and 5.&#160;&#160;United States defined benefit pension expenses were reclassified to the Corporate segment from other operating segments as the plans were frozen as of April 30, 2009 and historical results were reclassified to conform with the presentation for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;The Ophthalmic Lens Processing segment manufactures and distributes computer-controlled production systems and aftermarket supplies sold to a diversified customer base in the ophthalmic industry.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Financial data for the fiscal years ended April 30, 2010, 2009 and 2008 for the Company's reportable segments are shown in the following tables.&#160;&#160;The accounting policies of the reportable segments are substantially identical to those described in the summary of significant accounting policies.&#160;&#160;The effects of material intrasegment and intersegment transactions have been eliminated.&#160;&#160;Asset information by reportable segment is not accumulated and disclosed, as it is not reported to the Company's Chief Executive Officer and is not used internally.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Future minimum rentals to be received under noncancelable subleases total $6.2 million.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company has two significant operating leases for facilities located in Connecticut and the United Kingdom.&#160;&#160;Each lease was originated under a sale-leaseback transaction.&#160;&#160;The Connecticut lease is a 17-year lease, entered into in the fiscal year ended April 30, 2002, and the United Kingdom lease is a 15-year lease, entered into in the fiscal year ended April 30, 2001.&#160;&#160;The United Kingdom lease contains a rent escalation feature that is accounted for on a straight-line basis over the contractual term of the lease.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In connection with the sale of ND Graphics, the Company remained a guarantor under a lease for ND Graphic&#8217;s headquarters facility in Toronto, Canada. This lease expires during the fiscal year ending April 30, 2018.&#160;&#160;The remaining undiscounted monthly lease payments were $2.3 million as of the sale date.&#160;&#160;The fair value of this liability of $0.7 million was recorded in Other long-term liabilities on the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The fair value of the $0.7 million liability was estimated using a probability based discounted cash flow analysis for the probability of non-performance by ND Graphics.&#160;&#160;The Company also holds a $1.0 million letter of credit to which the Company has immediate access to in the event of default by ND Graphics under that lease. The Company has recorded this letter of credit as an asset for $0.7 million in Other assets on the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;As of April 30, 2010, there was no existing default or indication of a prospective default by ND Graphics under the lease.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Note 19.&#160;&#160;Discontinued Operations and Asset Sales</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On September 1, 2009, the Company sold 100 percent of the capital stock of FOBA for a net sales price of approximately $8.8 million, net of transaction fees.&#160;&#160;FOBA was acquired in October 2008 as part of the acquisition of Virtek.&#160;&#160;Sales proceeds of approximately $0.9 million will remain in escrow for a two-year period for possible application to specified contingencies.&#160;&#160;A gain on sale of $1.7 million was included on the accompanying Consolidated Statements of Operations within Loss from discontinued operations for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On September 30, 2009, the Company sold substantially all of the assets and liabilities of ND Graphics for a net sales price of approximately $5.3 million, net of transaction fees.&#160;&#160;A loss on sale of $3.2 million was included on the accompanying Consolidated Statement of Operations within Loss from discontinued operations for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;ND Graphics will continue to serve as the Company&#8217;s Canadian distributor for its Sign Making and Specialty Graphics segment.&#160;&#160;The Company expects some continuing cash flows, primarily from sales of equipment and aftermarket supplies to ND Graphics, although these cash flows are not expected to be significant enough to preclude discontinued operations accounting.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The operations of ND Graphics and FOBA were not considered a core strategic focus for the Company.&#160;&#160;See Note 1.&#160;&#160;Net proceeds from the transactions were used to reduce the Company&#8217;s outstanding debt.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company allocated a portion of its interest expense to discontinued operations, as the proceeds from the sales were required to reduce the Company&#8217;s outstanding obligations under its credit facility.&#160;&#160;The Company allocated approximately $0.3 million of interest expense to discontinued operations for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2010, $0.6 million of interest expense for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2009 and $0.3 million for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During the fiscal year ended April 30, 2009, the Company sold the Ophthalmic Lens Processing segment's Australian facility for a sales price of $1.0 million.&#160;&#160;The Company realized a gain of $0.6 million related to this transaction, which was reflected as a benefit within Selling, general and administrative expenses on the accompanying Consolidated Statement of Operations for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During the fiscal year ended April 30, 2008, the Company sold its rights to its Ophthalmic Lens Processing segment's Innovations software product to Ocuco, Inc. for a sales price of $1.0 million.&#160;&#160;The Company received $0.2 million in cash and $0.6 million in notes receivable at the date of the sale.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Company received shares of preferred stock in Ocuco Holdings Limited, a private company.&#160;&#160;A gain of $1.0 million was reflected as a benefit within Selling, general and administrative expenses on the accompanying Consolidated Statement of Operations for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;&#160;The sale of these assets did not meet the criteria for the sale of a component of the Ophthalmic Lens Processing segment.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Also during the fiscal year ended April 30, 2008, the Company sold a non-operating unused parcel of land in Connecticut for a sales price of $1.4 million.&#160;&#160;The Company accounted for this transaction under the full accrual method.&#160;&#160;The Company received $0.3 million in cash and a note receivable for $1.1 million at the date of the sale.&#160;&#160;A gain of $1.3 million was recorded in Other income (expense), net on the Company's Consolidated Statement of Operations for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;The note receivable was collected in full during the fiscal year ended April 30, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For the fiscal years ended April 30, 2010, 2009 and 2008, stock options to purchase 1.9 million, 2.0 million and 0.7 million shares of common stock, respectively, were excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share because the exercise price of the stock options exceeded the average market price of the Company's common stock.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Note 21.&#160;&#160;Subsequent Event</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On June 8, 2010, the Company approved plans to consolidate its Massachusetts-based Gerber Innovations business, a business unit of the Sign Making and Specialty Graphics segment, into an existing Connecticut facility, with an expected completion date of September 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;As a result of the consolidation, the Company expects to generate annualized savings of approximately $0.9 million.&#160;&#160;The Company estimated the costs related to this facility consolidation to be approximately $1.1 million, the substantial majority of which will require the outlay of cash.&#160;&#160;The Company expects that $0.3 million of these costs will be restructuring charges related principally to employee severance costs and $0.2 million will relate to lease contract termination costs.&#160;&#160;Other costs are expected to be non-severance employee costs of $0.4 million and moving expenses of $0.2 million.</font></div>

<br>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">These costs are expected to be incurred during the fiscal year ending April 30, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On June 16, 2010, the Company approved plans to align the Gerber Innovations business under the management of the Apparel and Industrial segment from the Sign Making and Specialty Graphics segment.&#160;&#160;This change is not expected to have a significant impact on segment disclosures.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Note 22.&#160;&#160;Quarterly Results (Unaudited)</font></div>
